alignments.note: עוֹד rendered by the fixed adverbial phrase *As yet*; headed on *yet*, the word carrying the lexeme (rule 24), with *As* the English phrase's connective.

The 1cs suffix on עוֹדֶנִּי is the verse's only first-person subject morpheme; the ASV realizes it twice, once in the main clause and again in the comparative clause *as I was*, so both *I*s form one discontinuous unit under rule 25, headed on the first. The competing reading marks the second *I* `added` under rule 17, but rule 25 gives a resumed subject to the morpheme that denotes it.
Verbless clause: the construction-supplied copula *am* joins the predicate adjective under rule 20, headed on *strong*. The unit is discontinuous around the comparative *as* (rule 25).

כַּאֲשֶׁר is one compound rendered by the correlative pair *as ... strong ... as*; both English words belong to the one connective's discontinuous unit on rule 14's reasoning for a correlative pair, and the source head is the governing opening morpheme כְּ under rule 23. Headed on the closing *as*, which carries the comparison's own relation, exactly as rule 24 heads *more than* on *than*; the competing reading heads on the opening *as*.
The article takes the demonstrative *this* the ASV writes in its place (rule 41); no demonstrative pronoun stands in the phrase to claim it.
Noun.

The comparative clause is verbless and its only predicate is the prepositional phrase, so the supplied copula *was* joins the preposition heading it under rule 49, headed on *in*. Competing reading: fold *was* into the gapped predicate חָזָק under rule 34; that adjective already holds its own *am*, so the copula is placed on the clause's own prepositional predicate.
יוֹם is a construct (Ncmsc) and can carry no article, so the ASV's *the* is supplied on it under rule 29.

The infinitive construct recast as a finite temporal relative clause takes the subordinator *that* together with the verb, exactly as rule 52 leaves *when they shall make* to the infinitive of בְּיוֹם הֵעָשׂוֹתוֹ where the preposition and the construct noun each already hold an English word. Discontinuous around the subject *Moses* (rule 25).
Direct-object marker with no English of its own; the ASV writes the object bare (*sent me*), rule 16.
Object suffix on the marker, rendered *me* (rule 18).
Proper name.
Comparative כְּ → *as*.
Noun.
Possessive suffix → *my* (rule 18).

Verbless clause whose remaining predicate anchor is the temporal adverb; the construction-supplied copula *was* joins it under rule 20 and the unit heads on *then*. The כְּ beside it already holds its own *as* and is not a home for a second word (rule 51).
The waw takes the *even* the ASV wrote for it; the corpus aligns a waw to *even* in 179 units (rule 14).

The second comparative כְּ takes the *so* of *even so*, each morpheme holding the word written for it (rule 2); reading *even so* as one fused rendering of the waw would leave this preposition unrepresented beside it.
Noun.
Possessive suffix → *my* (rule 18).
Parallel to the *was then* clause: the supplied copula *is* joins the temporal adverb predicate under rule 20, discontinuous around the subject noun phrase (rule 25), headed on *now*.
Preposition → *for*.
The article assimilated into the pointed preposition is a real token (rule 12); the ASV writes *for war* with no *the*, so it is unrepresented (rule 29).
Noun.
Conjunction → *and* (rule 14).
The לְ before the infinitive construct takes the written *to* (rule 52).
יָצָא → *go out*; the particle completes a lexeme *go* alone does not write, so it stays with the verb, headed on the verb (rule 44).
Conjunction → *and* (rule 14).
The לְ before the infinitive construct takes the written *to* (rule 52).
בּוֹא → *come in*; the particle completes the lexeme and stays with the verb, headed on the verb (rule 44).

review_notes: The verse's two comparative frames were placed by the morphemes actually written: כַּאֲשֶׁר carries the correlative *as ... as*, and in the second frame the waw takes *even* while the second כְּ takes *so*.

Both supplied copulas in the כְּכֹחִי clauses were placed on the temporal adverbs אָז and עַתָּה as the clauses' remaining predicate anchors (rule 20); the copula of the *in the day* clause was placed on its prepositional predicate under rule 49.
The resumed *I* of *as I was* is given to the 1cs suffix of עוֹדֶנִּי under rule 25 rather than marked `added`.
